title: Cancellation Compliance for Regional Gym Chains
one_liner: A drop-in cancel-and-freeze portal that meets each state's auto-renewal rules and writes straight into the billing system.
customer: Regional gym and studio chains with 10-300 locations still using in-person or certified-mail cancellations, and franchisors.
problem: The FTC's national click-to-cancel rule was vacated in July 2025, but enforcement continues (the FTC sued Fitness International/LA Fitness over cancellation hurdles), state auto-renewal laws demand online cancellation if you joined online, and New York City's own click-to-cancel rule takes effect October 1, 2026. Chains run legacy contracts and billing where cancellation is manual, so exposure is AG settlements and class actions.
solution: A white-labeled 'Cancel, Pause, Downgrade' portal with a jurisdiction rules engine (notice periods, save-offer limits, refund proration, confirmations) that writes to the chain's billing platform through API or RPA, with audit logs and legally bounded retention offers.
why_now: NYC's October 1, 2026 deadline, the FTC's restart of subscription rulemaking, and active state AG scrutiny create a dated trigger with budget.
revenue_model: $150-400 per location per month plus $2k setup; share of saved revenue on approved retention flows.
non_obvious_insight: Compliance opens the door, retention pays for it: a compliant flow with legally allowed save offers often lifts net retention versus the friction chains use today, so the CFO buys it. The moat is the multi-state rules matrix plus billing-system integrations.
first_30_days: Build a rules matrix for 10 states plus NYC with a consumer-protection lawyer, sell a $1k mystery-shop 'compliance scan' of each chain's cancellation flow to 20 regional chains, and convert two into design partners.

title: Fish Settlement Audit Becoming the Fleet's Payment Rail
one_liner: Start by auditing settlement sheets against fish tickets to recover missed money, then become the split-pay rail that routes each settlement to crew, lessors, lenders and the IRS.
customer: Skippers and permit holders who pay $99 flat or 15% of any recovered amount for the audit. Crew use the shares calculator free. Later, skippers and quota lessors pay about 0.3-0.5% of settlement flow for split-pay, and lenders and CFEC-adjacent programs pay referral fees.
problem: The 'price' you're paid is a stack: base price, quality bonuses (for example $0.15 RSW, $0.05 bleeding, $0.05 chilling), loyalty or volume bonuses, post-season retros, and deductions for ice, fuel, gear advances and storage. Every processor's sheet looks different. The fisherman's own copy of the fish ticket sits in a Ziploc in the wheelhouse and never gets matched against the settlement. Nobody checks. Then the whole lump lands in one skipper's account weeks later and he has to act as the bank for crew shares, quota lease payments, loan payments, gear vendors and self-employment tax. That is where disputes, missed quarterly taxes and stiffed crew come from.
solution: Audit: photograph the settlement sheet and fish tickets, and an LLM parses pounds, price stack, bonuses and deductions, flags weight mismatches, missed quality bonuses, wrong grades and unexplained deductions, and prints a plain-English 'you were owed' letter. A crew shares calculator generates crew settlement sheets from the skipper's expense rules. Rail: once trust exists, route the settlement into a virtual account that auto-splits per signed crew share agreement, quota lease, loan payments, vendor invoices and a tax set-aside, with instant partial payments.
why_now: Final settlements for the 2026 salmon season are landing right now (Oct-Dec). Price swung from $1.03 to $1.72 in one year, so fishermen are checking. Vision LLMs can read messy sheets at near-zero cost. Banking-as-a-service and real-time payment rails make split-pay possible for a small team. Crew who waited about four years for crab disaster relief also learned that clean earnings paperwork is worth money.
revenue_model: Audit: $99 flat or 15% of recovery. Rail: 0.3-0.5% of settlement flow plus interchange and float. Later: earned-wage advances against booked settlements, lender referrals, claim-packet prep for federal disaster relief (crew earnings vaults double as the proof), and an anonymized price tape sold to buyers and lenders.
non_obvious_insight: The skipper is the fleet's unlicensed bank, and nobody has both documents in one place. The audit is the trojan horse: it gets a fisherman to hand over settlement history, which is exactly the underwriting and routing data needed for the rail. The settlement sheet is a stack of price components, and the money is hidden in the parts nobody reads.
first_30_days: Post in fishermen's Facebook groups: 'free settlement check, send the sheet.' Process 100 sheets by hand plus LLM, log every error found, and turn 5-10 recoveries into case studies. Build the crew share calculator as a free viral wedge. Charge 15% of recovered amounts above $500. Start collecting the anonymized price stack by port, species and processor.

title: Concession-Adjusted Comps for Appraisers
one_liner: A browser tool that reconstructs what homes really sold for after seller credits and buydowns, so appraisers, lenders and AVMs stop valuing collateral off gross headline prices.
customer: Independent residential appraisers and small appraisal firms in high-concession metros (Atlanta, Austin, Dallas, Phoenix, Florida) first; then appraisal management companies, HELOC/home-equity lenders and AVM vendors.
problem: Redfin reports 44.7% of Aug 2026 sales carried seller concessions (Atlanta 72.8%) while national price indices still show +3.7% YoY. The recorded price is gross; the credit or rate buydown lives in MLS remarks, agent notes and the Closing Disclosure. Appraisers are expected to adjust comps for concessions but have no reliable data, so they burn hours phoning agents, and collateral values drift above true net prices.
solution: A Chrome/desktop add-on that runs inside the appraiser's own MLS session. It uses LLM extraction over listing remarks, price history and agent notes to estimate concession type and dollar value (closing-cost credit, 2-1 buydown cost, permanent points), asks the appraiser to confirm with a one-click agent email, and writes a supported adjustment into the sales-comparison grid. Confirmed records build a cooperative net-price database, later licensed as an index and API.
why_now: Record concession share with 30-year rates near 7.5% has made seller-funded buydowns a de facto financing product. Structured appraisal reporting makes concession fields explicit, and LLMs only recently became reliable at parsing messy MLS remarks.
revenue_model: $49-79 per appraiser seat per month; site licenses for AMCs and lenders; net-price index and API licensed to AVM vendors and home-equity portfolios ($0.10-0.50 per lookup or an annual data license).
non_obvious_insight: Sellers defend the headline price and negotiate the credit, so the true markdown is invisible in every public index and owned by nobody. Appraisers feel this pain daily, which gives a labeled, growing dataset for free and a wedge into lenders whose collateral models are quietly overstated.
first_30_days: Recruit 15 appraisers from state appraiser groups in Atlanta and Austin. Ship a remarks-parsing concession worksheet as an MVP with a 2-week trial, then charge $49 per month. Publish a monthly 'net vs recorded price' note for five metros to get press and lender attention. Stay within each appraiser's own MLS license and do no bulk scraping.

title: Independent Auditor for AI-Scribed Billing
one_liner: A continuous, coder-signed check on whether ambient AI scribe notes actually support the E/M levels being billed, before the payers or the government find out.
customer: Compliance officers, CFOs and revenue-integrity leaders at health systems and physician groups (20-500 providers), MSOs and PE-backed groups that rolled out ambient AI scribes. Secondary buyer: acquirers doing diligence on scribe-enabled practices.
problem: After ambient scribe rollouts, E/M distributions shift toward 99204-5 and 99214-5. Studies of six health systems show high-acuity visit share up roughly 12-20 points for new visits. Payers respond with AI downcoding and record requests, and the False Claims Act exposure is real if notes carry exam elements or time statements that did not happen. The scribe vendor cannot credibly audit itself, and annual compliance audits of 5-10 charts per provider cannot see systemic drift.
solution: Step 1 is a claims-only drift diagnostic (no EHR integration): compare each provider's E/M and modifier distribution before and after go-live with specialty benchmarks and peers, and rank the provider outliers. Step 2 is a targeted sample review by certified coders of the flagged encounters, checking that MDM or total-time really support the level. Copied-forward text, unsupported time attestations and orders without documented reasoning are the failure patterns. Step 3 is a continuing dashboard plus quarterly audit memos designed to be shown to a payer, auditor or the OIG. It includes a payer downcoding forecast.
why_now: Ambient scribes went mainstream across health systems in 2025-26. Research is documenting the coding-intensity increase and describing a payer-provider 'coding arms race', and payers are turning to their own AI for downcoding. The OIG's compliance program guidance expects organizations to audit new technology used in billing. Nobody independent has a standard offering yet.
revenue_model: $8-15 per audited encounter, or $15-30 per provider per month for the drift monitor plus sampled audits. Enterprise annual contracts of $50-200k. Diligence engagements at $10-25k each.
non_obvious_insight: The risk is not template bloat that scribes create in the HPI and exam. Under the 2021 E/M rules those elements do not count toward the level. The risk is that the scribe's fluent narration makes medical decision making and time statements sound stronger than what the physician did, and audits succeed or fail on MDM and time. Only coders who have survived payer audits know this. That is why a coder-signed audit is worth more than a model score, and why a compliance officer needs a third party, not the scribe vendor's coding module.
first_30_days: Find 3 mid-size groups, ideally with 30-100 providers, that adopted a scribe in the last 12 months, through LinkedIn outreach to compliance and revenue-integrity leads. Offer a free claims-only drift diagnostic, since 12 months of CPT data from their billing system is enough. Show them the outlier providers. Convert to a paid sample-audit engagement ($10-25k) and a monthly monitor. Recruit two certified auditors (CPC, CPMA) as contractors.

title: Verifier-Ready Emissions Data Rooms for CBAM Exporters
one_liner: A metering-to-evidence pipeline that gives small non-EU steel, aluminum and fertilizer producers a clean, pre-audited data room for accredited verifiers, so their EU and UK buyers stop defaulting to punitive default values.
customer: Producers and processors with 50-500 employees in Turkey, India, Egypt, Vietnam, Ukraine and South Africa (steel re-rollers, extruders, wire and fastener makers, fertilizer blenders). Paid by the producer or subsidized by the EU/UK importer buying from them.
problem: CBAM entered its definitive phase in 2026 and UK CBAM starts 1 Jan 2027 across 8 sectors. Importers lacking actual emissions data fall back on default values, which carry a mark-up (background, verify). Accredited verifiers are scarce, and small producers keep energy invoices in spreadsheets with no monitoring plan, so verification is slow and expensive and importers cannot get usable data.
solution: A two-week onboarding: connect electricity and gas meters or invoices, production logs and precursor traceability, then generate the monitoring methodology plan, the emissions report in CBAM format and an evidence index. Internal pre-verification, hand-off to partner verifiers, quarterly refresh, and sharing of the verified data with each importer through an API.
why_now: The definitive period began in 2026, verification of 2026 imports lands in 2027, and UK CBAM begins in three months. Default-value cost pressure now exceeds the price of proper data collection.
revenue_model: EUR 6-25k/year per plant (producer-paid or importer-sponsored supplier program) plus a coordination fee per verification.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone sells CBAM to the EU importer's finance team. The bottleneck is evidence-poor factories and verifier capacity upstream. Importers will fund supplier readiness because default values cost more than the tool, and verified plant data is reusable across every EU and UK customer of that plant.
first_30_days: Find three EU or UK importers of steel wire or fasteners with Turkish or Indian suppliers (trade fairs, LinkedIn) and offer a supplier-readiness pilot for five plants at EUR 3k each. Deliver with templates and spreadsheets and partner with one or two verifiers.

title: Settlement Back Office for Farm Water Conservation
one_liner: Program administration as a service that enrolls small farms in paid fallowing and conservation programs, verifies acre-feet with satellite evapotranspiration plus meter data, pays within 14 days, and hands the farm's CPA a clean tax packet.
customer: Payers: irrigation districts, state and basin conservation programs, corporate-funded coalitions and cities buying temporary leases, who pay the admin fee. End users: family farms of 50-800 irrigated acres in the Colorado River basin.
problem: The 2027-2036 framework pushes the next cuts onto agriculture, which takes about 70% of the river. Buyers want verified acre-feet at a price per acre-foot. Farmers want simple metering and fast payment, and fear that fallowing weakens their water right. Amazon's $20M ($32M raised toward a $100M goal) shows demand with no settlement layer. Programs run on spreadsheets and site visits, so small farms wait months and mis-report the income.
solution: A portal that enrolls farms and sets a consumptive-use baseline from public field-scale ET data, pump-power meter data and the farm's own records. Local crop advisors are paid per visit to verify. Contract templates carry a 'right-protection' letter agreed with the state water agency. ACH payment in 14 days. Automatic W-9 and 1099 handling, plus a tax and books packet on income timing and conservation-payment treatment for the farm's CPA. Funders get an audit-ready acre-foot ledger.
why_now: Interior issued the Record of Decision in Aug 2026 with Powell and Mead at about 36% of capacity. 95% of the basin is in drought. Corporate and public conservation money is arriving with no back office. Free satellite ET data and cheap power-meter telemetry now make remote verification credible, and LLMs make program-specific agreements and tax packets cheap.
revenue_model: 3-5% of disbursed funds as a program admin fee. $150 per farm onboarding fee, paid by the program. Later, a spread on instant-pay float. A $100M coalition goal at 4% is about $4M of admin revenue.
non_obvious_insight: Water markets fail at settlement and trust, not price discovery. A farmer will fallow if he is paid in weeks and his water right is legally shielded. The winning product is paperwork plus a legal shield letter plus a tax packet, not a marketplace. The customer who pays is the funder who would otherwise have to staff a program office.
first_30_days: Approach 3 irrigation districts or NGOs running conservation pilots and offer to administer 20-40 farms for a flat pilot fee. Build the enrollment form, an ET baseline report from public data and ACH payout in 30 days. Sign an LOI with one coalition partner. Recruit an agricultural CPA and a water attorney as advisers to draft the shield-letter approach.

title: Mailed Proof Books for Grandparents Who Buy Prints
one_liner: Turn a wedding gallery into a personalized printed booklet, mailed to each grandparent and parent with a phone number to order prints, because the people who actually pay for wedding prints never click gallery links.
customer: Wedding photographers (they pay only via revenue share). The end payers are the couple's parents, in-laws and grandparents, who spend $150-400 per household on prints and albums.
problem: The dirty secret of studio economics is that couples buy almost nothing after delivery. They have the gallery and Instagram. The people who buy prints and albums are mothers, mothers-in-law and grandparents, and the photographer's only delivery channel is a link emailed to the couple, who rarely forward it. Pic-Time and similar platforms added face-recognition and selfie-search galleries in late 2025, but that assumes a phone-comfortable guest willing to scan their face on a website. Grandma will not do that. Every wedding leaves an estimated $500-2,000 of print revenue uncollected, and the 'last photo with Grandpa' has a clock on it.
solution: The photographer uploads the gallery and the family list (they already have it from the formals shot list). We cluster faces, have the photographer confirm the 6-12 key elders and parents, and auto-build a 16-24 page softcover booklet per person ('Nana's Book: 22 photos of you and your grandkids'). We print and mail it within about 10 days of gallery delivery, with the couple's opt-in and a handwritten-style note from them. Every booklet carries a QR code plus a toll-free number answered first by a human and later by a voice agent that takes orders by phone and card, with check-by-mail as an option. Orders are fulfilled through pro labs, and the photographer sees a dashboard of sales.
why_now: AI face search has just become standard in photographer gallery platforms (Pic-Time's Nov 2025 update), which proves photographers will pay for AI galleries but leaves the elder channel unserved. Softcover print-on-demand now lands at roughly $6-10 for a 24-page book via lab and POD APIs. 2026-grade voice agents can take a print order from a 78-year-old who hates websites. Wedding-guest demographics are also aging, since couples are marrying later and grandparents are still at the table.
revenue_model: No upfront fee to the photographer. We front the booklet cost (about $10 landed) and keep roughly 40% of resulting print and album order revenue at lab retail, with the photographer keeping 60%, which is pure incremental margin. Optional $15 flat per-booklet pricing for photographers who want to buy outright.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is not the client. The couple's inbox is the wrong channel, and a personalized object with the recipient's own face on it is something people do not throw away. The product is a channel to 60-85-year-olds who respond to paper and phone calls, and the gallery software is just the data source.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 photographers from local and online groups who delivered a wedding in the last 6 months. Produce booklets for 2 of their weddings each, at your cost (about $100 in print and postage per wedding), using a Pic-Time/ShootProof export, open-source face clustering (InsightFace) and a lab or Lulu/Blurb-style API. Route the phone number to the founder's cell. Track orders per booklet. If 1 in 5 booklets converts to a $100+ order, sign the rev-share terms and scale to 50 studios.

title: Tamper-Proof Photo Evidence for Produce Rejections
one_liner: A capture-only app that produces AI-proof receiving-dock photo and video evidence so shippers can contest bogus load rejections and reroute rejected produce to salvage buyers within hours.
customer: Mid-size grower-shippers and brokers of berries, leafy greens, tomatoes and other perishables (Salinas, Yuma, Nogales and Florida corridors). PACA-licensed receivers who want to prove genuine rejections are a second segment, and produce factoring companies a third.
problem: Produce is sold before it arrives, and when market prices fall, a rejection on 'condition' photos is a well-known way to force a price cut. Shippers have photos, phone calls and slow inspections. Generative editing makes photos cheap to fabricate or alter, and neither side can prove authenticity (IC3 notes many victims cannot tell AI was involved). Rejected loads then rot or are dumped because salvage rerouting is slow, adding to food waste.
solution: In-app capture only, with device attestation, GPS, server timestamp, pallet-tag and lot-code OCR, Bluetooth temperature-logger tie-in, a standard shot list built from USDA quality standards, and a signed content-credential manifest. Each load gets a shareable verification link that both parties, a USDA or third-party inspector and PACA arbitrators can open, plus a live tele-inspection mode. Once a rejection is verified, an eight-hour clock starts and alerts go to salvage buyers, processors and food banks.
why_now: By 2026 photo editing with generative tools is trivial and undetectable to most people. The farm labor shortage means late harvests and more variable quality. The EU is moving toward binding food-waste cuts (30% in retail by 2030), which makes measured diversion valuable. Content credentials and device attestation are now standard on phones.
revenue_model: $4-8 per load or $400-1,500 a month per shipper, a 5-8% fee on the recovered value of rerouted salvage, and a co-sell with produce factors who freeze advances during disputes.
non_obvious_insight: In produce, a bad photo is a price-negotiation weapon, and whoever controls the trusted photo controls the money. The wedge is the shipper and the factor, who lose most from doubtful rejections, not the receiver. Verified evidence also turns each rejection from a bargaining event into clean market data.
first_30_days: Offer a free 30-day pilot to 3 grower-shippers in one corridor and capture their next 100 loads. Measure dispute-resolution time before and after. Recruit a produce factoring company or PACA attorney as a co-seller. Build the shot list from USDA grade standards.

title: Virtual Detention Basin from Smart Cisterns
one_liner: Thousands of backyard tanks that pre-drain before forecast storms, coordinated like a virtual power plant for stormwater.
customer: Stormwater utilities and sewer districts under combined-sewer consent decrees, and cities running basement-flooding programs.
problem: Utilities spend billions on tunnels and tanks to control overflows and basement flooding, while private-lot storage sits unmanaged because each barrel is dumb. FEMA money is unstable, so cities want cheaper capacity.
solution: Forecast-controlled cisterns and rain gardens with low-cost cellular valves that pre-drain ahead of storms and hold water at the peak, driven by AI weather ensemble forecasts. The utility pays per managed gallon at peak. First product is a 200-tank pilot in one sewershed, retrofitting existing barrels with a roughly $150 controller.
why_now: AI weather ensembles (operational since 2025) make per-storm control affordable, cellular valves are cheap, and consent-decree deadlines and unstable FEMA funding push cities toward distributed capacity.
revenue_model: Per managed gallon or per tank-year utility contracts, plus grants and rebates covering hardware.
non_obvious_insight: A city's cheapest new detention basin is 10,000 backyards coordinated like a virtual power plant.
first_30_days: Identify 3 combined-sewer cities with rebate programs, retrofit 50 existing barrels with controllers, and measure peak outflow reduction.

title: Shopfloor Pulse: Voice-Agent Census of Job Shops
one_liner: Voice agents phone thousands of US machine shops monthly, publishing a real-time index of lead times, backlog and price pass-through.
customer: Macro and industrial hedge funds and alt-data desks, OEM sourcing chiefs and defense primes, PE and search funds hunting retiring owners, and regional economic developers.
problem: ISM surveys purchasing managers, not job shops, and MMS admits no dataset exists on shop ownership or retirement. Buyers cannot see real capacity or lead times, and funds rely on lagging government and PMI data despite July PMI at 55.6, prices at 71.1 and 12.64M jobs.
solution: Compliant, disclosed voice agents call about 3,000 shops a month with a four-minute script: quote lead time on a standard part, backlog weeks, materials surcharge, 5-axis or Swiss availability, and owner sale intentions. Combine with web and state-registry data. Publish a monthly index by region and process. Sell it as a subscription, and sell the resulting capacity directory to sourcing teams.
why_now: Voice models are cheap and natural in 2025-26, volatility makes non-consensus data valuable, and the retirement wave makes shop-level data valuable to buyers.
revenue_model: Alt-data subscriptions at $30-150k a year. Directory seats at $500-2k a month. Lead sales to search funds.
non_obvious_insight: The industrial base is tens of thousands of small firms nobody surveys, and the cost to survey them fell roughly 100x. A regional index that beats ISM by weeks is valuable because it is early, not because it is big. Telemarketing and TCPA rules need legal review, and calls should start human-assisted.
first_30_days: Build and legally review the script. Call 500 shops across three clusters. Publish a free preview index. Approach 10 alt-data desks. Aim for three paid pilots at $25-50k by month six.

title: Duty Refund Claims Desk for Small Importers
one_liner: Over $100B in tariff refunds are flowing, but small importers can't afford the paperwork. Run the filing, deadline tracking and refund advance as a service.
customer: Small and mid importers of record ($1M-$50M of annual imports) that paid the struck-down tariffs, plus customs brokers who don't want the grunt work.
problem: Refunds are flowing but small importers face records, liquidation and protest deadlines, multiple brokers and bonds, and filing costs ('not without a cost,' Colorado Sun, 2026-07-02). The government is fighting an order to refund all importers (WaPo, 2026-08-11). Brokers are paid per entry, not per refund, so nobody chases.
solution: Connect customs-entry data from the importer's broker, identify eligible entries and deadlines, file protests and post-summary corrections through a partner licensed customs broker, and track each claim to payment. Offer an advance of about 80% of approved claims at a discount, funded by a small credit facility.
why_now: Refunds have passed $100B (CNBC 2026-08-07, Forbes 2026-09-09) with litigation ongoing. Twenty-five states are challenging the replacement Section 122 tariffs, so a second claim wave may follow.
revenue_model: 10-15% success fee on recovered duties, plus a 2-3% monthly discount on advances once financing is in place.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck isn't law, it's data assembly and deadline hygiene. The refund often lands in a broker's account or gets stuck for lack of a clear owner. Small importers who recover cash are also the source of pass-through claims for the downstream-recovery business.
first_30_days: Sign a licensed customs broker as partner. Recruit 20 importers through marketplace-seller communities and manufacturer associations. Process five entries by hand end to end and collect the first success fees.

title: Step-Up Basis Files for Inherited Assets
one_liner: Sell CPAs and estate lawyers a cheap, defensible date-of-death valuation packet for every inherited house or portfolio.
customer: CPAs and enrolled agents preparing 1040s and 1041s for heirs, estate attorneys, and heirs selling inherited homes or securities.
problem: The step-up in basis (IRC 1014) is the biggest tax break most families receive, but only if the heir can support date-of-death value. Below the estate-tax threshold no appraisal is required, so heirs sell years later with no valuation and risk the IRS asserting the parent's low original cost. Securities and crypto also need clean date-of-death pricing.
solution: A $150-$400 per-asset packet: houses (AVM plus retrospective appraiser sign-off), securities (date-of-death pricing), crypto, collectibles. It outputs a Basis Memo for the CPA's file, stores it, and alerts the heir when the property lists for sale.
why_now: The higher federal exemption (reported $15M) means fewer estates file a Form 706 that would have documented values. Home prices are sharply higher than a few years ago, so embedded gains are large. Boomers are the source of most transfers.
revenue_model: Per-report fees, CPA firm subscriptions, and appraiser marketplace margin.
non_obvious_insight: The tax benefit is lost through missing paperwork, not law. A small, cheap document created at death protects a large tax saving years later.
first_30_days: Sell to 15 CPA firms and 5 estate attorneys. Use an AVM API plus 3 contract appraisers per metro. Deliver in 5 business days and gather feedback on what the CPAs actually attach to returns.

title: Allergen Drift Alerts for School Cafeterias
one_liner: A weekly diff engine over the open Open Food Facts and USDA Branded Food Products data that tells school nutrition directors when a product on their order guide silently changed its allergens.
customer: K-12 school district food service directors and their purchasing co-ops and state agencies (about 13,000 US districts). A parent-facing paid alert tier for families of children with severe allergies is a secondary market.
problem: Distributors substitute products and manufacturers reformulate without notice. After sesame became the ninth major US allergen, some bakeries began adding sesame on purpose. Directors keep allergen lists in spreadsheets built from last year's spec sheets. Recalls are announced only after exposure, and cooks get blamed for what is really supplier drift.
solution: Ingest the district's order guide (Sysco, US Foods, Gordon Food Service item lists) and match SKUs to GTINs. Track ingredient statements and allergen declarations over time using Open Food Facts revision history and the monthly USDA Branded Food Products (GDSN) releases. Send a weekly 'allergen drift' report and immediate alerts when an allergen is added, a 'may contain' changes, or a substitution appears. Auto-update the district's allergen matrix and menu labels.
why_now: Branded-food data goes stale quickly and USDA now publishes monthly GDSN updates. Reformulation churn following the 2023 sesame rule and supply-chain substitutions is high. Open Food Facts has reached scale, and diffing it is cheap while no one sells the diff.
revenue_model: USD 500-1,500 per district per year, tiered by SKU count. State-agency or co-op bulk licenses. Parent alert tier at USD 3-5 per month.
non_obvious_insight: Most cafeteria allergen incidents trace to a silent supplier change, not to cooking error, so the value is monitoring the upstream data exhaust that already exists and is free. Directors will pay for peace of mind and liability evidence, not for a new database.
first_30_days: Build the diff pipeline for the 300 most common K-12 SKUs. Publish a free weekly 'Allergen Drift Report' newsletter aimed at food service directors and state school nutrition associations to build trust. Offer 5 districts a free SKU-matching of their full order guide. Convert to paid alerts with the first two districts that catch a real change.

title: Retiring Masters' Exit Interviews, Funded by Employers and AI Labs
one_liner: Capture the last generation of unrecorded tradespeople as expert playbooks for their employer and consented, royalty-bearing training data for robotics and industrial-AI labs.
customer: Two payers. Operations and HR leaders at municipal water and wastewater utilities, electric co-ops, machine shops and food plants pay $6-15k per retiring expert. Robotics and maintenance-copilot companies pay to license consented expert demonstration data.
problem: Decades of tacit knowledge walk out the door with baby-boomer retirees: why a pump sounds wrong, how to set up a difficult mold, what to check third when the obvious fixes fail. Written SOPs miss it. Robotics labs can buy cheap novice chore video but have almost no expert-grade manipulation and diagnostic-reasoning data, and crowd-sourced gig filming is hitting a quality ceiling.
solution: A two-person crew, or a mailed camera kit plus a remote interviewer, spends 2-3 days per expert: head-mounted and wrist cameras during real tasks, think-aloud narration, 'what would you check next?' probing, and staged edge cases. Deliverables: (1) an employer-owned playbook of video-indexed SOPs, fault libraries and decision trees, plus a searchable Q&A bot; (2) a de-identified dataset licensed to AI and robotics buyers. The expert gets a retention bonus and a royalty share, and the employer gets a discount in exchange for licensing rights.
why_now: The physical-AI and humanoid boom created a 2025-26 scramble for demonstration data, and large labs and gig apps now pay people to film chores. Chore data saturates quickly, so experts are the next scarce input. The skilled-trades retirement wave is peaking. Maintenance and diagnosis copilots need reasoning traces, not just video.
revenue_model: Employer capture fee of $6-15k per expert; dataset licensing at roughly $100-500 per hour of expert footage with recurring buyers; a follow-on 'build your maintenance copilot' project; royalty pass-through to experts as the trust mechanism.
non_obvious_insight: The highest-value physical-AI data is not being crowd-sourced. It sits in the heads and hands of people who were never recorded, and their employers will pay to capture it for their own continuity reasons. That makes the training data a subsidized by-product, undercutting gig-data vendors on cost and beating them on quality. Royalty-sharing with the expert defuses the consent and labor fight that will otherwise hit the data industry.
first_30_days: Choose one vertical, either municipal wastewater operators or CNC machinists. Recruit 5 soon-to-retire experts through state rural-water associations or machining trade newsletters. Run two paid pilots at a $2.5k intro price with a $400 camera kit. Cut a 20-hour sample reel and send it to 10 robotics and industrial-AI startups to collect letters of intent.

title: Payday-Shaped Pix Automático Cadence for Low-Income Billers
one_liner: A layer on top of Brazilian gateways that designs the recurring-debit cadence (weekly, biweekly, payday-aligned) and consent options at enrollment, so small billers stop losing all-or-nothing monthly debits.
customer: Small Brazilian businesses billing low-income or irregular-income payers on a recurring basis: neighborhood ISPs, small gyms, neighborhood schools, discount-card clinics, motorbike-rental fleets for delivery couriers (to validate first), and insurance or consórcio sellers. They pay 10-15% of incremental collected revenue.
problem: Pix Automático collects the full amount or nothing, with no partial debits. Retries are limited to 3 in 7 days and only if the payer consented. The payer can cancel or edit the mandate up to the eve of the debit, and the mandate cannot change frequency or amount ceiling after authorization. Meanwhile 83.9 million Brazilians were in negative credit standing in August 2026, a record. Monthly lump debits collide with irregular income, and small merchants still chase payers by hand every month.
solution: At enrollment, quote cadence from the payer's income rhythm (weekly for app-paid couriers and informal workers, biweekly for 'vale' and salary splits, monthly for salaried payers) and create the correct mandate with retries-consent and, optionally, credit-line consent. A WhatsApp 'pre-debit rescue' 48-72 hours before each charge lets the payer confirm, move the date to just after payday, pause, or split into a new mandate, instead of silently cancelling in the bank app. Built as an API layer over a gateway that already exposes the retry policy, such as Asaas. Reports per merchant show debit success rate, cancellation reasons and recovered revenue.
why_now: Pix Automático launched in June 2025 and adoption is compounding. Companies had to be able to offer it from 1 Jan 2026, and it is far cheaper than cards and has no chargebacks. About 60% of low-income Brazilians lack credit cards, so account-debit is the only recurring rail for that segment. Most tooling so far is generic dunning, not cadence design.
revenue_model: Performance-based: 10-15% of incremental collected revenue versus the merchant's baseline, or a flat R$149/month for merchants who prefer subscription. Later a per-debit micro-fee and a marketplace of payer-side 'payday buffers'.
non_obvious_insight: The frequency is locked at authorization, so cadence is an irreversible, high-leverage decision at signup, and nobody optimizes it. Because partial collection is not allowed, the only way to fit a low-income payer's cashflow is to change the shape of the debits, not to chase them afterwards. Evidence: PagBrasil reports +182% transactions and +181% new users quarter over quarter from Q4 2025 to Q1 2026, and a coffee subscriber cut churn 25.2% and cost 50% versus cards (https://www.pagbrasil.com/blog/recurring-payments/automatic-pix-2026/). Serasa reported 83.9 million negativados in August 2026 (https://www.shipay.com.br/inadimplencia-no-brasil-como-melhorar-cobrancas/). Rules on no partials, 3 retries in 7 days and cancellation until the day before are at https://celcoin.com.br/articles/vale-a-pena-pix-automatico/ and https://docs.asaas.com/docs/faq-2. The mandate 'cannot change the frequency' and 60% of low-income Brazilians lack cards (https://www.pymnts.com/news/payments-innovation/2025/pix-automatico-debut-opens-brazils-recurring-payments-market-to-millions/). Small billers describe the monthly grind: 'Todo mês alguém precisa lembrar o cliente, mandar mensagem, enviar chave Pix, cobrar boleto atrasado' (https://www.alfadenegocios.com.br/2026/08/pix-automatico-para-pequenos-negocios.html).
first_30_days: Days 1-3: Confirm in the BCB spec which recurrence periodicities are permitted (weekly and biweekly are assumed, not yet verified) and the per-debit fee, since more frequent debits cost more per charge. Fall back to monthly with payday-aligned dates plus split mandates if not. Days 4-15: Build a thin layer over the Asaas API and a WhatsApp pre-debit rescue flow. Recruit 10 merchants from a single vertical, ideally neighborhood ISPs or courier motorbike-rental fleets, through their ERP user groups and Facebook groups. Days 16-30: Run a split test (monthly vs payday-aligned vs weekly) on new enrollments, report debit success and cancellations, and sign the first 3-5 performance-fee contracts.

title: Flat-Fee Estate Close-Out Pods for Middle-Class Heirs
one_liner: A retired probate attorney supervises 2-3 junior associates and an AI workflow to close $200K-$2M estates for a flat fee, filling the gap between a $400/hr attorney and nothing while giving locked-out grads a paid apprenticeship.
customer: Executors and heirs of middle-class estates (a house plus retirement accounts), often a grieving widow or an adult child. Channels: funeral homes, hospice social workers, credit unions and elder-law referral networks. Flat fee of about $3,500-6,500.
problem: Wealth managers chase the top 2% of households who hold $62T of the wealth transfer. Middle-class estates get either a $400/hr lawyer or an overwhelmed amateur executor, and probate takes 9-18 months (unverified practitioner claim). Online will sellers treat probate as an add-on. Meanwhile entry-level paralegal, analyst and ops roles that used to train juniors are vanishing (Stanford: 22-25-year-olds in exposed jobs 19% below trend).
solution: A 'pod' is one supervising attorney (owning the firm, or operating in a jurisdiction that allows non-lawyer ownership such as Arizona ABS or the Utah sandbox), 2-3 estate associates (laid-off analysts, HR, bank-ops people or grads), and AI workflows for asset discovery, creditor notices, date-of-death valuations, account-closure kits and the final accounting. Each pod runs about 25 estates at once. The heir gets one coordinator, a weekly 15-minute call and one checklist. Associates keep a verifiable log of completed estate steps that ladders to paralegal or licensed-paraprofessional status (AZ, UT, WA, OR, MN).
why_now: Deaths are flat (3.07M in 2024) but dollars per estate are rising, and the first wave of transfers is spousal (about $40T heads to widowed women). AI now handles document drudgery well enough to cut hours per estate from a couple hundred to a few dozen, which turns a not-worth-a-lawyer's-time market into a viable flat-fee product. State regulatory sandboxes are more open to new legal service models than ever.
revenue_model: Flat fee, median about $3,900 with tiers by complexity and state. Target 60%+ gross margin at 25 concurrent estates per pod. Channel partners get flat, bar-compliant marketing fees or co-branded membership benefits (not per-referral fees, which most states bar for lawyers).
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck in estates is not legal knowledge. It is 100-200 hours of tedious, deadline-driven admin that nobody will pay $400/hr for and no algorithm can be trusted with alone. AI collapses the hours enough to make flat pricing work, and the supervised junior is the feature, not a cost, because employers now refuse to train them.
first_30_days: Sign one retired probate attorney in one county (probate is local). Hire two laid-off analysts. Get 3 funeral homes and 2 hospice social-work teams to hand out a one-page 'first 30 days after a death' checklist with a booking link. Price at $3,900, run 10 estates in 90 days on a manual playbook, then automate the steps that repeat.

title: Insurer-Backed Self-Certified Permits for ADUs
one_liner: Japan-style private building confirmation: AI code review plus a licensed private reviewer plus an insurer-backed compliance warranty, so an ADU or small addition gets a certified package in about 48 hours where state law allows private providers.
customer: ADU builders, residential designers and architects, and homeowners in states with private-provider or third-party review statutes (Florida first), later cities piloting insured expedited review.
problem: Honolulu residential permits average 218 days (commercial 469). Government AI tools serve reviewers, and applicant-side tools for ADU owners, small builders and rural jurisdictions are thin. Faster review even increases filings (+34%) faster than permits issued (+5%).
solution: An applicant-side pre-clearance engine reads the plan set, runs the jurisdiction's zoning, structural and energy rules, and returns a correction list in minutes. A licensed private provider signs, and a surplus-lines policy from an MGA indemnifies owner and jurisdiction against code errors, priced from the engine's error data. Where private-provider laws exist the package is submitted directly, and elsewhere it is offered as an insured fast-track pilot.
why_now: Government pilots prove review can be automated (Honolulu review cycles down 58%, Denver's $4.6M contract). LLMs can now read plan sets. The ROAD Act funds standard blueprints. Insurers are hunting for new specialty lines, and applicants are desperate.
revenue_model: $1,500-3,000 per ADU permit package. 10-15% share of warranty premium. SaaS for designers.
non_obvious_insight: Governments will never build the applicant-side tool because of conflict of interest, but insurance can do what regulators cannot: price and carry the residual risk that a bad plan slips through. Japan has let designated private bodies issue building confirmations since the late 1990s, and permit timelines there are days, not months.
first_30_days: Partner with a Florida private-provider firm. Run 20 ADU and remodel plan sets free for three designers and compare predicted corrections to actual city comments. Pre-sell to ADU builders at $1,500 and show the accuracy data to two MGAs.

title: Night Shift Tox Bulletin for Opioid Settlement Counties
one_liner: A no-patient-data network where rural ER nurses text in what they are seeing, turned into weekly local drug-supply alerts sold to counties spending opioid settlement money.
customer: County opioid settlement councils and public health departments, EMS medical directors, jails, harm-reduction programs and rural hospitals. Paid by county contract from opioid settlement funds.
problem: New adulterants show up in a rural ER as a pattern before they show up in any dataset. Examples are patients who are sedated but not responding to naloxone, or patients with a slow heart rate and low blood pressure that is not the usual opioid picture, or brutal withdrawal with high blood pressure. Confirmatory lab results take weeks or months. Surveillance networks are concentrated in academic and urban centers, so a rural county may learn about something two states over long after the ER has seen it. Nurses talk to each other in the break room and on private Facebook groups, but they have no safe way to alert the county, EMS, jail or harm-reduction workers. Hospital administrations do not want a nurse speaking for the hospital.
solution: A 30-second SMS or Signal report with no patient identifiers: date, county, number of patients, presentation flags, response to reversal, what the patients said they took, and any new physical findings such as wounds. Reports are aggregated with a minimum threshold (for example 3 or more per week) to protect privacy. The service returns a plain-language weekly county bulletin to nurses, EMS, jail medical staff and harm-reduction groups, and triggers targeted drug-checking or lab testing of residue with a lab partner. Include a jail-specific alert because withdrawal from newer sedatives is dangerous inside a jail.
why_now: Medetomidine, a veterinary sedative, is now in the illicit supply well beyond Philadelphia. Wastewater data showed it in at least one of 14 states every week from October 2025 to January 2026, and California published an emerging issue brief in April 2026. The main ER sentinel program has only about 17 to 20 academic centers, so rural emergency departments are barely covered. Tens of billions of dollars in opioid settlement funds are arriving in local hands, and county councils are actively looking for evidence-based data and surveillance projects.
revenue_model: $12-36k per year per county or multi-county region, with a lower price for small counties and bundled state contracts through state opioid settlement offices. A secondary product is a per-test fee when the network triggers drug-checking or lab confirmation, and a jail early-warning subscription.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing is not lab capacity. It is a trusted channel for the person who sees it first and has no authority to speak. A night-shift nurse is a better early-warning sensor than a dashboard, and the data is qualitative and deliberately human: 'this doesn't look like what we normally see.' Because you can build it with no PHI, nurses can contribute from their own phones off shift without touching hospital systems. Other tools (ODMAP, poison center feeds) are built for incident counts and law enforcement or EMS reports, not clinical pattern recognition.
first_30_days: Recruit 25 rural ER and night nurses from state nurses' groups and private Facebook communities. Send a free weekly bulletin to three neighboring counties and their EMS agencies. Attend an opioid settlement council meeting (agendas and minutes are public) in one of them. Offer a paid six-month pilot at $1,000 per month. Line up one lab partner for confirmatory testing. Get a lawyer to review the no-PHI reporting language and publish a clear policy telling nurses to leave out anything identifiable.

title: Lead-Refund Recovery for Home-Service Pros
one_liner: Auto-dispute junk paid leads from Google Local Services, Angi, Thumbtack and Yelp, and take a share of the credits recovered.
customer: HVAC, plumbing, roofing, locksmith, garage-door, pest and electrical firms with 3-30 employees spending $2k-30k a month on paid leads.
problem: A large share of paid leads are spam, wrong-service, out-of-area or duplicates (typically cited at 20-40%; prior knowledge). Disputes are manual and deadline-bound, so owners rarely file. Getting customers is the top small-business challenge, so the spend is untouchable but the waste is fixable.
solution: Connect ad and lead accounts and the phone system's call recordings. Transcribe and classify each lead against each platform's dispute reasons, file disputes with evidence inside the window, track credits, and flag chronically junky sources. A monthly report shows net cost per real lead.
why_now: Cheap call transcription and LLM classification make per-lead review nearly free, and legacy local-marketing vendors are shrinking and raising prices, which raises the value of every recovered credit.
revenue_model: 20-25% of credits recovered (no credit, no fee), or $99/month per account.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody sells lead-refund recovery because each dispute is worth $30-150, but automation turns them into a portfolio. Recovered credits are pure margin for the owner.
first_30_days: Ask 10 contractors from local trade Facebook groups for 90 days of lead exports and call logs. File disputes manually to learn acceptance rates, then automate the top three reason codes.

title: Depot Finder for Robotaxi Fleets
one_liner: A power-first site database and brokerage matching robotaxi fleets to half-empty garages, office podiums and big-box lots with unused electric service.
customer: Robotaxi fleet operators and their depot partners (AV company real-estate teams and fleet contractors such as Moove, Avis and Lyft's Flexdrive) in launch cities, and owners of distressed garages and office podiums.
problem: AV fleets need charging and cleaning depots near service zones with megawatts of power and workable zoning, while utility interconnection takes 18-36 months. Meanwhile downtown garages and office podiums have oversized electrical service and falling parking revenue.
solution: A ranked site database using proximity to service zones, available service capacity (utility maps and permits), zoning and neighbor tolerance. We broker the lease, run pre-development diligence and later sell a 'depot-in-a-box' kit.
why_now: Waymo and others have announced 2026 expansion to many more metros using fleet partners, interconnection is the chokepoint, and office and parking distress is deep.
revenue_model: Broker fee of 4-6% of first-year rent, $5-10K per month site-package subscriptions from fleets, and landowner listing fees.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource is electric service already in place, and 'obsolete' vacant buildings hold plenty. The best robotaxi real estate may be a half-empty garage with a multi-megawatt service, not airport-adjacent industrial land.
first_30_days: Compile 300 candidate sites in two launching metros. Call the local depot leads at fleet operators and deliver a 'power-ready shortlist' for $5K. Sign one or two exclusive landowner listings.

title: Contest-Proof Signing: Capacity Sessions for Wills
one_liner: A recorded, clinician-run capacity and intent session at will signing, so a later contest by disappointed heirs has strong evidence against it.
customer: Estate-planning and elder-law attorneys and RIAs whose clients are 75+, in blended families or making unequal bequests. Clients pay the clinical entity directly, and firms bundle it into fixed-fee packages.
problem: An older wealthy cohort, more second marriages and rising dementia diagnoses mean more disputes about capacity and undue influence. Evidence of capacity at signing is usually the drafting lawyer's memory plus boilerplate. That is weak in court and expensive to defend.
solution: A standardized signing-day product. A licensed geriatric psychiatrist or neuropsychologist runs a structured, recorded interview with validated screening, an independent private conversation without family, and a recorded 'why I chose this' statement. The bundle is hashed and stored under the attorney's privilege, with an optional yearly refresh and in-home or remote delivery.
why_now: FDA cleared blood tests for Alzheimer's pathology in 2025, so more people get an early diagnosis and want to sign while they still can. Remote notarization and e-will laws widened access, and video is cheap. The transfer is concentrated in older households with complex families.
revenue_model: $700-$1,500 per session billed by the clinical entity, firm-level packages of $25K/year, and yearly refresh sessions. Lawyer referral-fee rules make direct client billing the safer structure (check state ethics rules).
non_obvious_insight: Capacity is a moment-in-time question and the evidence is manufactured at the signing. It is cheap to create then and impossible to recreate later. Diagnosis awareness is creating a rush window nobody is serving.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 geriatric psychiatrists or neuropsychologists per metro. Partner with 5 elder-law firms. Run 20 sessions at $900 and have each firm's litigators review the artifact bundle. Keep clean records of what each session found.

title: Succession Roll-Up for Retiring Solo Therapists
one_liner: A service that brokers and buys retiring solo practices and transitions clients to vetted associates, so clients are not orphaned and young clinicians inherit a full caseload.
customer: Retiring psychologists, social workers and family therapists (paid through fees and earn-outs) and early-career clinicians or group practices paying a transition fee, roughly $3-10k per practice.
problem: A large share of independent therapists are past 55, and solo practitioners typically just close, leaving clients scrambling. New clinicians spend 12-24 months building a caseload. Consolidation is capturing platform-dependent supply (Spring Health acquiring Alma, Jan 2026; Universal Health Services buying Talkspace for $835M, Mar 2026), but nobody owns practice transition the way dental service organizations do.
solution: A 6-12 month warm-handoff program consistent with ethics codes and client choice: records custody, client consent workflow, payer-panel reassignment through a group NPI, referral-source handover, and an earn-out to the retiring clinician funded by the successor's collections. Software handles consent, records and payer onboarding. Later: an MSO owning the transitioned practices.
why_now: Back-office rails built by Alma and Grow (Grow raised $150M) now make onboarding an associate cheap. Boomer therapists retire through 2025-30, and platform consolidation leaves the independent tail unowned.
revenue_model: Transition fee (5-10% of annual practice revenue), earn-out spread, later MSO margin, and buyer-side subscription.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone is consolidating the platform, but nobody is consolidating the goodwill of retiring clinicians, which is the cheapest source of established caseloads and referral relationships and the one asset that walks out the door every Friday.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 retiring clinicians through state association mailings and Psychology Today profiles. Match five with early-career clinicians. Have a healthcare attorney draft an ethics-reviewed transition agreement, and complete two transitions at a flat $3k each.

title: Withholding-Credit Reconciliation for Indonesian Sellers
one_liner: Reconcile marketplace-withheld tax against annual returns for the many small sellers across Shopee, TikTok Shop and Tokopedia.
customer: Indonesian SME marketplace sellers and the bookkeepers who serve them.
problem: Indonesia starts marketplace tax collection on Oct 1 and has cut de minimis to $3. Sellers on several platforms will see withheld amounts on payouts, and matching those to annual filings creates over- and under-payment risk.
solution: Ingest payout statements and withholding proofs by API or WhatsApp forward, reconcile per platform, flag threshold crossings and generate return workpapers. The wedge is a white-label tool for accountants who serve seller communities.
why_now: The Oct 1 start date forces this pain within a quarter. Details of the rules should be verified before building.
revenue_model: Rp99-299k per month per seller, or an accountant white-label licence.
non_obvious_insight: Platform collection makes compliance visible, and a seller's first pain is reconciling rather than filing. The accountant channel is fragmented and unserved.
first_30_days: Support one platform's statement format and recruit 50 sellers through seller WhatsApp groups.

title: Contingency Hunters for Unbilled Water Revenue
one_liner: Find the 'ghost parcels' and slow big meters that leak revenue out of a utility, using assessor rolls, building footprints, imagery and billing data, and get paid 20-30% of what is recovered so the city risks nothing.
customer: City, county and district water and sewer utilities with 10k-200k connections. The buyer is the finance director or utility director who is facing a council fight over the next rate increase.
problem: Utilities are raising rates 5-10% a year to fund PFAS treatment, lead line replacement and aging pipes, and councils are pushing back on affordability. Meanwhile revenue leaks out in places nobody owns: structures with no water account (unpermitted ADUs on shared meters, converted garages, fire and irrigation taps never billed), commercial compound meters that are 20-30 years old and under-register at low flows, meters swapped without the account being updated, stopped or zero-read accounts that never get investigated, and sewer-only accounts billed off a bad water read. The customer information system, the GIS parcel layer and the assessor roll sit in different departments. Nobody owns the join, and nobody has staff to do it.
solution: Join the utility's account list and consumption history to the assessor roll (building sq ft, units, use code), permits, open building-footprint datasets and aerial imagery (pools, irrigated area, added structures). Build an expected-consumption model by parcel. Rank the mismatches: no account at all, consumption far below expected, sudden step-downs after a meter change, and large meters whose low-flow profile looks wrong. A small field crew and a meter-test partner verify the top leads. The utility gets a documented recovery list with legal-ready evidence, back-billing calculations that respect the state's limits, and a meter-replacement plan. The firm takes 20-30% of first-year recovered incremental revenue.
why_now: Rate shock and affordability politics in 2025-26 make 'recover what we're owed before raising rates' an easy story for council. Open building-footprint datasets and cheap vision AI make expected-consumption modeling accessible to a two-person team, and utilities that finished smart-meter rollouts now have interval data that has never been analyzed for revenue. Contingency work also clears procurement easily because there is no upfront cost.
revenue_model: Contingency of 20-30% on the first 12-24 months of recovered annualized revenue, plus a fixed fee for a meter-testing and replacement plan. Later, a recurring SaaS monitor ($1-3 per 100 accounts per month). Optional referral fees from meter and test vendors.
non_obvious_insight: The leak that matters is not in the pipe. Large commercial meters are about 10-20% of accounts but 40-60% of revenue, and the oldest ones quietly under-register the low flows that hospitals, hotels and factories use all night. The utility never sees this loss because the meter is the thing measuring it.
first_30_days: Pick a county whose assessor roll and building footprints are downloadable and whose utility publishes or will release account addresses (public-records request). Run a free scan and generate 20 named addresses with expected versus billed usage. Cold-email finance directors at five utilities with 'we'll show you 20 unbilled addresses before you sign anything'. Sign the first contingency contract with a city that has a rate hearing scheduled, and verify leads with a hired meter-testing subcontractor.

title: Install Clubs: Brazilian Consórcio for Home Contractors
one_liner: A contractor-anchored, interest-free buying pool: 60-200 homeowners pay monthly into escrow and each month a few move up the queue (by draw or bid) to get their roof, heat pump or solar+battery installed.
customer: Independent home-service contractors (roofing, HVAC/heat pump, solar+storage, windows) with 5-50 staff who want pre-sold backlog. Their end users are homeowners who have been quoted $8-20k and don't want a 9-12% HELOC or home-improvement loan.
problem: Big-ticket home upgrades stall on financing. Contractors burn 10-20% of revenue on lead gen and lose many quoted jobs because the homeowner can't or won't borrow. The 25C/25D federal credits ended for installs after Dec 31, 2025, so the effective price jumped overnight.
solution: Software + bank escrow + a lawyer-drafted prepaid-service template that lets a contractor run a 'club' for one product (e.g., a $9k heat-pump install). Members pay $100-200/month into segregated escrow. Every month one or more members are allocated an install by lottery or by bidding extra to jump the queue. The contractor is the counterparty and delivers at a locked price, so there is no loan and no interest. The platform earns an administration fee instead of interest, as Brazilian consórcios do.
why_now: Brazil's consórcio system hit a record 12.76M active participants and about R$500B of credit sold in 2025, in a high-rate environment, so the model is proven when loans are expensive. In the US the 25C/25D credits vanished on Dec 31, 2025, rates are still high, and the only consórcio-style player I found (NWX) sells general credit letters for real estate and vehicles. Nobody has wrapped the pool around a service the seller delivers.
revenue_model: Administration fee of roughly 8-12% of contract value collected in monthly installments, a SaaS fee per contractor club, and a share of escrow float yield.
non_obvious_insight: A consórcio is not a loan, it is a queue with a price guarantee. Making the licensed contractor the counterparty turns the pool into a prepaid-service escrow (like layaway) instead of a credit product, which sidesteps most lending regulation. The contractor gets what it wants most: scheduled backlog, cash before work, and near-zero CAC because 'your neighbor's roof gets done this month' recruits the next member. Homeowners who were declined or scared off by loans are the fastest-filling segment.
first_30_days: Sign 2-3 contractors in one state. Get an escrow account at a community bank and a prepaid-service agreement drafted by a lawyer who knows that state's home-improvement deposit rules. Mine each contractor's list of past quotes that never closed and pre-enroll about 40 members in a 'Founders Club' at about $150/month for a $9k install. Run the first allocation in month 2, so the first installed job and first admin-fee revenue land by around day 60.
